title: How to Export Logs from OpenSearch
content_md: Pull documents with the _search API, or let a short Python script page through them with helpers.scan. If your pipeline kept the original log line, usually in message or event.original, extract just that field and you get the raw logs back. OpenSearch Dashboards can generate reports from saved searches, but not in a format LogTotal reads today. OpenSearch backs a lot of homegrown SIEMs and log platforms, including Amazon OpenSearch Service and the Wazuh indexer. Prime Core has 23,466 detection rules for OpenSearch, mapped to 671 MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Below is how to get a clean slice of data out, sanitize it, and investigate it for free in LogTotal. Get Started For Free Before you start Permissions. With the security plugin enabled, your role needs read access on the index pattern: the read action group, or at least indices:data/read/search* and indices:data/read/scroll*. On Amazon OpenSearch Service, that’s either a fine-grained access control user or IAM credentials with SigV4 signing. Find the right fields. Index patterns differ between pipelines. Check one document and the mapping before you write a query: GET logs-*/_search?size=1 GET logs-*/_mapping You’re looking for the time field (@timestamp or timestamp) and, ideally, a field that holds the original line (message, event.original, full_log in Wazuh). Count first. Run GET logs-*/_count with the same query to see what you’re about to pull. The commands below follow the OpenSearch 2.x documentation, checked October 2
